body.statement: For every \(Q\in\mathfrak F(P)\) and every family of ordinary versions \(\{\kappa^d_{Q,v}\}\) satisfying single-world factorization and reached-history modularity, there exists a simultaneous completion \(\{\bar\kappa_{Q,v}\}\) on every legal parent configuration such that \(\bar\kappa_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid d,u)=\kappa^d_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid u)\) on every positive-probability parent fiber, \(\bar\kappa_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid d,u)=\bar\kappa_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid d',u')\) whenever \((d,u)\sim_v(d',u')\), and \(Q(O^d=x)=\prod_{v\in\mathcal V_d}\bar\kappa_{Q,v}(x_v\mid d,x_{\operatorname{pa}_d(v)})\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(x\in\Omega\). Thus all-fiber agreement is a selectable version completion, not an additional causal-model restriction.
body.justification: The lemma separates harmless null-fiber version selection from the substantive global response-system lift.
body.gap: RichardsonRobins2013SWIG constrains the FFRCISTG model on realized single-world distributions; the finite equivalence-class completion needed for an explicit dormant-coordinate construction is usually left implicit.
body.consumer: The projection-and-lift theorem can use common dormant-fiber kernels without presenting that choice as a strengthened causal assumption.
